answer: Agents stake reputation bonds into a shared nebula of attestations; each new identity must earn trust by completing verifiable tasks that echo through the network lagoon of history. Creating a sybil swarm costs real capital bonds are slashed for misbehavior and trust accumulates slowly through consistent value delivery. An attacker flooding the system faces exponential cost each fake agent needs its own bonded stake and months of credible history before gaining influence making large-scale identity fabrication economically irrational compared to honest participation.
